touches.text: A row number is the same on every box. Storing a memory first reserves its slot from the librarian on the home box (CAIRN_HOME_HOST, 6.3.7.4), so two boxes are never handed the same slot, and the slot stays reserved until the write is complete. If a box's list is shorter than the slot (eg it holds rows up to 100 and is handed 123 while a sync is bringing the rest), it adds the open slots in between as blanks, and the sync fills them in as it proceeds. WHY: node ids are in every link and blob pointer, so a row has to mean the same node everywhere.

ADDRESS: every reference is one 64-bit integer, the top 16 bits a table tag and the low 48 a row. A list of addresses can name nodes, blobs, leaves in any tree, lists and links. Every pointer is a direct row fetch, and a new kind of thing is a new tag, not a schema change.

Deposit. A hit reinforces: the string's words are added to the counts along the path it took. With `for <device>/<question>` (8.4.4) the same happens in that device's tree, so two holders of one question drift apart in weights by what each has seen.

chain: the grammar every chart stage speaks. WHY: one grammar lets stages chain in any order. USERS: CodeMother (heaviest), base, tester, rehearsal, build_inspector, proof_coverage, aider, skills/chart.
